record.paper_title: Open Problems in α Particle Condensation
record.context_brief: Hoyle-like α-gas states in heavier A = 4n nuclei
record.original_question: Which heavier self-conjugate A = 4n nuclei beyond ¹²C, such as ²⁰Ne, ²⁴Mg, ²⁸Si, or ⁴⁰Ca, possess dilute α-gas condensate states near their nα disintegration thresholds, and can experiments excite and identify them through large-amplitude breathing modes or soft Coulomb-explosion modes?

evidence.quote: One may reasonably think that also 20Ne, 24Mg possess α gas states. The Ikeda threshold [11] increases fast though: 19.17 MeV for 20Ne, 28.48 MeV for 24Mg, 38.46 MeV for 28Si, etc.

If the experimenters were able to excite those nuclei into a large amplitude breathing mode, at some point surely they would cluster into a coherent state of α particles. Eventually for n = 8 - 10 α’s there will not exist a Coulomb barrier any longer and the condensate gas will start to expand coherently as a soft Coulomb explosion mode.
A dream may be to dissociate 40Ca into 10 α’s.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A self-conjugate nucleus of mass number A = 4n (with n a positive integer) is one composed of n protons and n neutrons in equal numbers (e.g., ¹²C, ¹⁶O, ²⁰Ne, ²⁴Mg, ²⁸Si, ⁴⁰Ca). The nα disintegration threshold (Ikeda threshold) of such a nucleus is the minimum excitation energy required to dissociate the nucleus into n free α particles; representative values are approximately 7.27 MeV for ¹²C, 14.44 MeV for ¹⁶O, 19.17 MeV for ²⁰Ne, 28.48 MeV for ²⁴Mg, and 38.46 MeV for ²⁸Si. By an "α-particle condensate state" of such a nucleus one means a 0⁺ excited state located near (typically slightly above) its nα threshold whose intrinsic structure is well approximated by n α-clusters occupying, with high probability, a single (lowest) 0S center-of-mass orbital — i.e., a dilute, gas-like Bose–Einstein-type condensate of α particles, analogous to the Hoyle state (the second 0⁺ at 7.65 MeV) in ¹²C.

Problem. 
(a) For each heavier self-conjugate nucleus with A = 4n and n ≥ 5 — in particular ²⁰Ne (n = 5), ²⁴Mg (n = 6), ²⁸Si (n = 7), and ⁴⁰Ca (n = 10) — determine whether there exists at least one 0⁺ excited state lying near its nα disintegration threshold whose wave function realizes a dilute α-particle condensate (an n-α gas) in the sense above.
(b) Identify experimentally feasible excitation mechanisms — in particular large-amplitude monopole "breathing" modes and, for sufficiently large n where the Coulomb barrier against simultaneous nα emission is expected to vanish (heuristically n in the range 8–10), a coherent "soft Coulomb-explosion" mode in which the condensate expands as a coherent n-α cluster — that can populate such states and allow their unambiguous identification through their nα decay channels.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent experimental and theoretical work has provided strong candidate evidence for a 5α condensate state in ²⁰Ne near 22 MeV (Nature Communications, 2023), and the 0₆⁺ state in ¹⁶O remains a strong candidate for a 4α condensate. For ²⁴Mg, ²⁸Si, and ⁴⁰Ca the existence and identification of nα condensate states is still considered an open experimental challenge, with only partial cluster-decay evidence available. Soft Coulomb-explosion identification for n = 8–10 has not been experimentally realized. Thus the question is partially solved: confirmed for ²⁰Ne, plausible for ¹⁶O, and open for heavier A = 4n nuclei.

status_evidence.title: The 5α condensate state in 20Ne
status_evidence.snippet: One excited 0+ state has a distinct gas-like characteristic and represents the 5α condensate state in 20Ne.
status_evidence.claim: A 5α condensate state in ²⁰Ne has been experimentally identified.

status_evidence.title: Status of Alpha-Particle Condensate Structure of the Hoyle State
status_evidence.snippet: Confirming the existence of Hoyle-analog states in Nα nuclei (N > 3) remains a major challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Identification of α-condensate analogs beyond ¹²C is an ongoing challenge.

status_evidence.title: Experimental investigation of α-condensation in light nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Experimental investigation of α-condensation in light nuclei beyond ¹²C.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental searches for α-condensates in heavier 4n nuclei are active and partially conclusive.

status_evidence.title: Alpha-particle decays from excited states in 24Mg
status_evidence.snippet: Alpha-particle decays from excited states in 24Mg studied; cluster decays observed.
status_evidence.claim: ²⁴Mg cluster decay studies provide partial information but no confirmed 6α condensate.
